emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the Supabase-specific setup before choosing Resend for Auth email.
emails.single_idea: Resend is available as a custom SMTP provider for Supabase Auth; its setup guide shows the connection, and Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit must also be adjusted for the expected signup volume.
emails.objection: “Does a custom SMTP provider actually change the limit affecting my Auth email?”
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend launched today or describe an undocumented new product release.
Do not promise that connecting Resend alone removes 429 errors; Supabase’s Auth limit remains separate.
Do not imply Resend Free has no daily cap or that any plan has unlimited monthly sending.
Do not promise to detect or prevent Supabase configuration wipes, or explain Supabase’s unexplained send accounting.
Do not claim this setup isolates transactional mail from marketing mail at the account or infrastructure level.
Keep Broadcasts, Automations, dedicated IPs, security claims, and customer testimonials out of this email.
Do not state or imply that every reader uses Supabase. Present this integration conditionally (for example, 'If you use Supabase...') unless the user-supplied campaign context establishes it.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The built-in sender’s email limit is separate from the Supabase subscription tier. Connecting custom SMTP also leaves Supabase’s initial Auth rate limit to adjust.
emails.mechanism: Configure Resend as custom SMTP for Supabase Auth using Resend’s documented setup, then review the Auth rate limit in Supabase’s dashboard.
emails.call_to_action: Read the Supabase SMTP setup guide — https://resend.com/docs/send-with-supabase-smtp
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether to configure Resend as the SMTP sender for this Supabase project.
emails.next_step_value: See the Supabase-specific configuration path and where to obtain the Resend SMTP credentials.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not change Supabase’s separate 30-message-per-hour initial Auth limit, establish the right Resend plan, or validate production delivery.

events.body:
Resend, our email sending platform for developers, is available as a custom SMTP sender for Supabase Auth.

If you use Supabase for signup, login, or password resets, you can route those emails through Resend. Our Supabase guide shows where to enable custom SMTP and where to get your Resend SMTP credentials.

Changing the sender does not remove Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit. After custom SMTP is enabled, Supabase initially limits Auth sending to 30 messages per hour. Review that setting against your expected signup volume before deciding whether to connect Resend to your project.
events.call_to_action: Read the Supabase SMTP setup guide

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Check Auth email headroom before launch"
events.subject: Check Auth email headroom before launch
events.preview_text: Compare daily and monthly sending limits before choosing an SMTP provider.
events.body:
If you use Supabase Auth, checking its logs can help investigate a 429 on an auth email. It still leaves you to choose and configure a custom SMTP sender if the built-in sender’s limit is too low.

Resend is available as an email sending platform for developers. You can connect it to Supabase Auth through custom SMTP for signup, login, and reset emails. Upgrading a Supabase subscription does not raise its built-in email sender’s limit.

Check the sender’s limits against the volume you expect. Resend Free includes 3,000 emails per month, capped at **100 per day**. Pro costs **$20 per month for 50,000 emails**, with no daily cap. Extra emails cost $0.90 per 1,000.

Free can also return a 429 when its daily quota is reached. Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit still needs to be set for your expected volume.

View pricing to compare the published allowances before choosing a plan.
